messages:
monitoring-bot: :rotating_light: ALERT: sudden surge detected on /v1/generate and /v1/embeddings from several IP clusters. 95th latency spike to 1200ms, 429s increasing. Aggregate RPS from suspicious ranges: ~4.2k. Potential automated scraping/contracted-tier abuse. root_ts=1769005555

sam: seeing the same in dashboards. free-tier tokens consumed fast, and some enterprise requests are hitting fallback. Is the impact user-visible? any 5xx?

maria: customer support: 3 tickets in last 10m, mostly 429s on embeddings. Enterprise A reported degraded streaming. No 5xx overall.

chris: quick triage: this looks like coordinated bursts hitting unauth routes and shared embedding cache. Could be credential stuffing or token reuse but pattern matches scraper UA + high concurrency. Suggest immediate controls: 1) tighten per-key concurrency 2) throttle anonymous/public endpoints 3) WAF rule to drop obvious bot UAs 4) route paid customer keys to dedicated capacity if possible.

sam: agree. Let's prioritize minimizing customer impact for paying customers. Who can apply WAF changes and flip the public embedding toggle?

kevin-sre: on it. Applying WAF rule now - targeting UA regex pattern: `(curl|python-requests|node-fetch|bot-|scraper)` and IP ranges: 198.51.100.0/24 + 203.0.113.0/24 flagged from logs.

kevin-sre: PATCH to WAF API:
```bash
curl -X POST https://waf.internal/api/rules 
  -H "Authorization: Bearer $WAF_TOKEN" 
  -d '{"action":"block","conditions":{"ua_regex":"(curl|python-requests|node-fetch|bot-|scraper)","ip_ranges":["198.51.100.0/24","203.0.113.0/24"]},"tags":["inc-1769005555"]}'
```

inc-bot: WAF rule created: id=9123 status=activating :hourglass_flowing_sand:

jia: Meanwhile I'm going to reduce free-tier burst window and enforce a hard per-key concurrency limit. Making a small runtime change to rate-limiter config in Redis. Applying delta: `burst_multiplier: 0.3 -> 0.1`, `max_concurrency_per_key: 20 -> 6` for free-plan.

sam: post the exact config blob so I can review quickly. If we drop too low we might trigger too many support tickets.

jia: config snippet being applied (redis keys: rate:plan:free):
```yaml
plan: free
  burst_multiplier: 0.1
  refill_rate_per_sec: 2
  max_tokens: 60
  max_concurrency: 6
```

maria: support: please prepare a canned response for free-tier customers about temporary quota limits due to abuse mitigation. I'll surface enterprise routing status to AEs.

chris: also toggling experimental feature `public_embeddings` to off for now — major source of scrape. Launch toggle command below.

chris: `POST https://flags.internal/api/toggle` payload:
```json
{"flag":"public_embeddings","active":false,"reason":"incident-1769005555 temporary disable to reduce scrape surface"}
```

kevin-sre: WAF rule 9123 is active. Early telemetry: 1.1k blocked requests in 3m from flagged UA patterns. Dropped 35% of scrape traffic.

jia: rate-limiter change deployed. Observing reduction in 429s for enterprise keys; free-tier 429s up (expected). Monitoring.

product-oncall: Notifying sales/support channels: enterprise customers should be routed to dedicated nodes. If anyone sees persistent impact for paid customers ping me and we can failover.

sam: can we do a quick fallback routing for VIP keys to dedicated pool? I can run the routing script.

chris: yes, run `scripts/route-to-dedicated --keys <list>` — make sure to add to `dedicated-override` cache with TTL 1h.

sam: running now for top 12 VIP keys. Log:
```text
[1769005940] routed key=acct_XXXX -> dedicated-pool-3 (ttl 3600s)
[1769005942] routed key=acct_YYYY -> dedicated-pool-3 (ttl 3600s)
```

maria: AEs have been updated. One enterprise reported improved perf after routing.

inc-bot: PAGE: on-call handoff scheduled. Current oncall sam -> jia at 1769007000 :bell:

sam: handing off. I'm stepping out for 20m to deal with a customer call. Jia, you're owner until 1769007000 + 30m. Please escalate to kevin if WAF/infra changes needed.

jia: got it. I'll keep monitoring metrics and adjust concurrency if we still see scraping. If needed we can enable geo throttle for certain IP ranges.

kevin-sre: one more mitigation: enable slow-salve token bucket for unauthenticated clients (limit to 1 req/sec) — I'll push a patch to rate-limiter redis script.

kevin-sre: redis lua snippet applied:
```lua
-- unauth token bucket
-- key: unauth:token:{ip}
-- rate: 1/sec, burst: 2
```

maria: support: preparing KB + status note. Tagging tickets with incident id INC-1769005555.

product-oncall: we've disabled `public_embeddings` and applied WAF blocks and quota reductions. Early indicators: overall RPS down 42%, 429s for free-tier up, enterprise latency back to baseline for routed keys. Good progress.

jia: monitoring shows new scrape sources spinning up different UA. WAF regex needs extension; adding heuristics for repeating prefix patterns and header anomalies. Will update rule 9123 to 9123a.

kevin-sre: updated rule 9123a. Additional ~600 blocks in 5m. Also added `rate-limit:referrer` rule to catch empty/referrer anomalies.

sam: excellent. Any customer-impacting actions we should communicate externally?

maria: yes — send an advisory to support: temporary stricter quotas on free tier and embeddings disabled until further notice. For enterprise: routed traffic and sorry for noise.

product-oncall: logging an incident ticket and scheduling a postmortem. Action items:
- WAF tuning owned by kevin-sre
- Rate-limit policy review owned by jia
- Postmortem writeup owned by sam
- Customer comms owned by maria

inc-bot: Incident INC-1769005555 created. Severity: S2. Postmortem task assigned.

sam: I'm back. Good job team, leaving handoff complete. If anything regress ping `#oncall` and I'll rejoin. :thumbsup:

jia: continuing watch. Will update if we need more aggressive measures (IP blackhole via cloud vendor, or rolling key rotations).

chris: after this stabilizes we should add automated runbook steps for contract-tier surges. I can draft one.

maria: thanks all. Closing thread for now and will update when postmortem is live.
